findings.summary: When no boundary is in the buffer yet, last_newline() returns index 0 (the leading CRLF), which is never deleted, so with chunked input the CRLF can leak into the field value.

judge.reason: Describes last_newline returning index 0 with leading CRLF, related to b1 but candidates empty, so cannot map; the claimed leak is a different symptom.

findings.summary: LINE_BREAK_RE.match(data) is used without a None check, so if the buffer doesn't start with a line break, .end() raises AttributeError instead of a clean ValueError.

judge.reason: Complains about missing None check on match, unrelated to the last_newline/find shortcut defect in b1.

findings.summary: The encoder writes the CRLF between headers and body only when the first Data event is non-empty, so if the decoder emits an empty first Data(b"", more_data=True), the CRLF is lost on re-encode.

judge.reason: Encoder empty-first-Data CRLF issue is unrelated to the answer-key bug and speculative.
